findings.title: Generating a 3.1.0 oracle and overlay does not clear the lane
findings.detail: The ruling is sound as a conservative early-warning policy, but new-minor onboarding needs an explicit decision. Executed b297de42c1146cb6e7132366cdd9f03e4400e6bb under pandas 3.1.0: it imports and completes make_oracle.py. Two independent processes produced identical 67,135-byte gzip payloads, SHA256 bc71c27de4ef992c75fdb79119939f9e360d23cb464e75cfffbd208f66cd95a2, containing 1584 encoder, 4620 temporal and 74 model cases. Generating its overlay produced Y=221, R=195, S=5. Comparing current code with that new pair still failed 72 temporal cases; every encoder and model comparison passed. For example, b297de4 reports transform/ValueError for p3-88, while current code succeeds with codes [0,1,2]. This branch deliberately leaves frozen transform failures unchanged. Thus adding both files is insufficient. A new oracle meaningfully records the counterfactual b297de4 behavior under new dependencies; it cannot honestly represent answers observed when H-0138 was decided. Recommend retaining that independent reference and leaving these 72 disagreements red pending an explicit disposition. Using current or newest released LizyML as the reference would change what the oracle proves and could bless the behavior being checked. Resolving that contract question is outside this review's authorized scope.

findings.title: The 185 differences need a representation-aware disposition
findings.detail: Reproduced all 185 differences against the 3.0.1 oracle plus overlay. They comprise 109 Timedelta unit/value changes and 77 stand-in-list changes, with one overlap. Every forward and reversed code array remains equal. The s44 input itself changes: pd.Timedelta(7, unit='D') has second resolution on 3.0.6 and microsecond resolution on 3.1.0; explicitly supplying the old second-resolution value removes that discrepancy. This agrees with the documented [pandas 3.1 resolution change](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/whatsnew/v3.1.0.html#datetime-timedelta-resolution-for-numeric-input). The other changes involve multiplied NumPy temporal units, whose construction also changed upstream. Repeating all 4620 temporal probes with the production needs_stand_in callback removed every stand-in and code difference; only 109 unit representations differed. Saved category JSON therefore changes for newly constructed inputs, but this is not evidence that LizyML must restore old predictions. All 185 affected production encoder states saved under 3.0.6 replayed under 3.1.0 with identical runtime and generated encoder codes, and their saved category JSON round-tripped through both codecs. Three representative tiny models—s44, p3-88 and p40-103—had identical booster hashes, categories and prediction hex values across the two environments. Full artifact-directory loading was not exercised because filesystem writes are prohibited. Record this classification before treating these differences as library regressions; do not normalize oracle answers merely to obtain green.

findings.title: The fallback needs job isolation and one validated artifact selection
findings.detail: Recommend LIZYML_H0138_ORACLE_MODE=latest-same-minor, set only on the latest job's pytest step. Before allowing either fallback or relaxed model checks, require GITHUB_ACTIONS=true and GITHUB_JOB=quality-latest-deps. Reject an enabled mode in any other job and reject unknown mode values; absence retains strict behavior. Test the flag accidentally set globally and in each blocking job. A flag alone does not satisfy DC1. Select an exact oracle first; otherwise use packaging.version.Version and choose the greatest older version with the same epoch, major and minor. Require its matching overlay; never mix versions or silently retreat from a corrupt or incomplete selected pair. Executed reference selection yielded 3.0.6→3.0.1, 3.0.1.post1→3.0.1, and 3.0.2rc1/3.0.2.dev1→3.0.1; 3.0.1rc1/dev1 and all tested 3.1 prereleases/dev releases had no eligible older oracle. Preserve suffix ordering rather than stripping it. Local builds also need a stated policy; full Version ordering selected 3.0.1 for 3.0.6+local. On fallback, meta pandas must equal the selected artifact version, both artifact versions must agree, and the runtime must satisfy the selection rule. Preserve count and known-ID checks. Compute the closed union from the selected frozen cases and use S_NAMED[selected_version], retaining duplicate-ID, before-outcome, Y/R/S membership and count assertions. Do not derive S from the overlay itself. Executed existing checks on 3.0.6 confirm the otherwise-surviving blockers: metadata AssertionError and S_NAMED KeyError('3.0.6').

findings.title: Skipping the model test bodies still executes all frozen models
findings.detail: The answers fixture computes models before the model test calls model_versions_match. Executed an in-memory prototype that changes the mismatch assertion to pytest.skip and selected only the o-object model test: pytest reported one skip, but the subprocess still computed all 74 models. An upstream model crash or timeout could therefore fail the shared fixture despite the intended skip. Decide model eligibility before fixture execution and tell the answers subprocess to omit models when ineligible, while still computing every encoder and temporal answer. On the latest lane, skip the 74 model cases and lane-version test when NumPy or LightGBM differs, including when pandas has an exact oracle; report selected oracle and expected/actual dependency versions. Matching dependencies must execute the model comparisons, and blocking lanes must retain failures on mismatches. This intentionally loses frozen model-regression detection while versions differ; fallback cannot be presented as complete model coverage. Add an always-visible terminal or CI summary, since the existing -q invocation does not display ordinary skip reasons: runtime versions, selected file paths/version, exact versus fallback, compared-case counts and skipped-model count.

findings.title: Close the Proposal acceptance list around the measured behavior
findings.detail: Recommend proceeding with the ruled same-minor policy, conditional on this closed acceptance list: (1) preserve all six existing frozen files byte for byte; (2) every blocking lane still fails without an exact oracle, including with the opt-in mistakenly set globally or locally; (3) exercise exact precedence, nearest older selection, numeric patch ordering, prerelease/post/dev/local policy, invalid versions, missing companions and corrupt metadata; (4) preserve every metadata and closed-union assertion against the selected version; (5) on the measured 3.0.6 environment compare all 1584 encoder and 4620 temporal cases, skip the 74 model cases plus version test with reasons, and execute zero model computations; matching model dependencies execute comparisons; (6) independently corrupt categories, mode, codes, stand-in state and a temporal expectation outside the overlay and demonstrate failures rather than skips; (7) pandas 3.1.0 with this tree must remain red with zero eligible same-minor comparisons—never silently compare against 3.0.1; (8) publish selection and coverage information even on green runs and preserve non-blocking job semantics; (9) define new-minor onboarding as independently generated, reproducible b297de4 oracle plus overlay, recorded environment/input provenance, a named S set, and explicit disposition of discrepancies such as the 72 measured here. Do not promise that artifact creation alone resolves the present 3.1.0 warning.

findings.title: The frozen-file and dependency measurements reproduce
findings.detail: Regenerated all three existing H-0138 oracles from b297de4 and all three H-0139 overlays: each matched its committed gzip bytes exactly. Printed lizyml.__file__ and dependency versions for every environment used. venvci is pandas/NumPy/LightGBM/PyArrow 3.1.0/2.5.4/4.7.0/26.0.0; venvlatest is 3.0.6/2.5.4/4.7.0/26.0.0. The targeted module on 3.1.0 without files reproduced exactly five failures and three empty-parameter skips. Redirecting reads to the unmodified 3.0.1 pair reproduced 77 failures/6206 passes on 3.0.6 and 262 failures/6021 passes on 3.1.0. The former failures are precisely 74 model version checks, the lane-version check, metadata and closed union. Exact 2.3.3 and 2.0.0 module runs passed 6508 and 6537 tests. The PyArrow claim also reproduced across pandas 3.0.1/3.0.6 × NumPy 2.4.2/2.5.4: all 1584 encoder cases matched with PyArrow; disabling PyArrow imports produced the same nine np.str_ category-type differences in every cell. Keep encoder comparisons active on dependency drift and record optional dependency presence/string-storage conditions in future generation provenance; pandas/NumPy/LightGBM versions alone do not describe all relevant conditions.

findings.title: No additional missing-per-version artifact mechanism was found
findings.detail: Executed the requested version-reference search using rg because this digest snapshot's Git index does not track its copied files, and searched frozen/golden/expected artifacts. Outside H-0138, the references are a pre-2.2 hashing branch, runtime-version recording assertions, pandas-major branches in H-0139/H-0141, and NumPy legacy-printing selection. They do not index missing patch/minor-specific files. The v0.17.1 persistence fixture's NumPy version assertion checks fixture provenance rather than the running NumPy version. Executed 549 focused category codec, generated codec and version-branch tests under 3.1.0 with no failures. Export tests requiring temporary files were inspected rather than executed. No second version-keyed frozen-file/table blocker was identified; this does not establish that every unrelated test passes.

findings.title: Historical firing rate and fresh resolution remain unverified
findings.detail: gh issue view for #389/#180, gh run list --workflow CI --limit 100, and gh run view 39766830320 failed to connect to api.github.com; browser access to the issues also failed. Consequently the posted issue/comment and historical 'every run' wording could not be independently verified. One cached latest-job log at /tmp/claude-1000/latest.log records the f002e8c PR merge, pandas 3.0.6 and the five oracle failures: one observed eligible fallback run, with no defensible historical denominator. Under the ruling, 3.0.6 compares 6204 encoder/temporal cases; current 3.1.0 compares zero because no same-minor pair exists. The 185-case measurement is a cross-minor diagnostic, not an allowed fallback. uv sync --upgrade --dev --dry-run --no-cache failed creating its temporary directory on the read-only filesystem, so installed venvci versions were verified but today's resolver was not rerun. The cached full-suite report matches the brief's 5 failed/16759 passed/255 skipped/30 deselected; the full suite was not rerun as instructed. All measurements were read-only: oracle paths and generator output were redirected in memory. The snapshot lacks generated lizyml/_version.py, so focused workspace-code runs loaded that metadata module from the supplied b297de4 worktree; printed library paths confirmed the code under test came from the workspace. No repository edits were made.
